description: A guide to the best beaches on Tamil Nadu's long coast: Chennai's city beaches, Kovalam (Covelong) and Mahabalipuram on the East Coast Road, Tranquebar and Velankanni on the delta coast, Rameswaram and Dhanushkodi, and Kanyakumari at India's southern tip, with the north-east monsoon, swimming rules and when to go.
dek: Tamil Nadu's coast is less about lazy beach days and more about temples, heritage and sunrise at land's end. Here are its best beaches and what each is for.

intro: Tamil Nadu has one of India's longest coastlines, running along the Bay of Bengal from Chennai down the Coromandel coast to Kanyakumari, where it meets the Indian Ocean and the Arabian Sea. Its best-known beaches are tied to temples and history: the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram, the Danish fort at Tranquebar and the tip of India at Kanyakumari.

The sea here is often rough, and swimming is prohibited on several city beaches, so plan beach time around walks, sunrise and heritage rather than long swims. The state gets most of its rain from the north-east monsoon, roughly October to December.
quickAnswer: The best beaches in Tamil Nadu are Kovalam (Covelong) near Chennai for surfing and its Blue Flag beach, Mahabalipuram for the Shore Temple, Elliot's beach in Chennai for evening walks, Tranquebar for its Danish fort, Rameswaram and Dhanushkodi for the ghost town at the end of the island, and Kanyakumari for sunrise at India's tip. Go from about December to March, avoiding the north-east monsoon.
takeaways: Swimming is prohibited at Chennai's Marina beach because of dangerous currents.
Kovalam (Covelong) on the East Coast Road is Tamil Nadu's surf town and has a Blue Flag beach.
Mahabalipuram's Shore Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage monument, stands on the beach.
Dhanushkodi, at the tip of Rameswaram island, has been a ghost town since the 1964 cyclone.
The north-east monsoon (about October to December) brings heavy rain and cyclone risk to this coast.

sections.heading: Chennai and the East Coast Road

items.name: Marina and Elliot's beaches
body: Marina, running along the city's shore, is one of the longest urban beaches in the world and fills up every evening with families, food stalls and kite sellers. Bathing is prohibited because of dangerous undercurrents. Elliot's beach at Besant Nagar is smaller and calmer, with cafes nearby.

items.name: Kovalam (Covelong)
body: A fishing village about 40 km south of Chennai with a point break, several surf schools and a Blue Flag beach. Not to be confused with Kovalam in Kerala.

facts.Best for: Surfing, a day out from Chennai

items.name: Mahabalipuram
body: The Pallava port town, about 55 km from Chennai, has the Shore Temple right on the beach, along with rock-cut monuments inland. Surf schools and seafood shacks line the village beach.

items.name: Tranquebar (Tharangambadi)
body: A former Danish trading post with Fort Dansborg on the sand and quiet streets of colonial houses, far from crowds.

items.name: Velankanni
body: A pilgrimage town whose basilica attracts visitors of all faiths; the beach is busy with pilgrims, especially during the annual feast in late August and early September.

items.name: Pichavaram
body: Not a beach but one of India's largest mangrove forests, near Chidambaram, explored by rowing boat through narrow channels.

items.name: Rameswaram and Dhanushkodi
body: Rameswaram is an island town reached by road and rail bridges across the Pamban channel. At its south-eastern tip, Dhanushkodi was destroyed by a cyclone in 1964; the ruins and the road to Arichal Munai, where land ends between two seas, are open to visitors in daylight hours.

image.alt: Pamban bridge over the sea to Rameswaram
image.caption: Pamban

items.name: Kanyakumari
body: At India's southern tip, where the Bay of Bengal, Indian Ocean and Arabian Sea meet, visitors gather for sunrise and sunset and take ferries to the Vivekananda Rock Memorial and the Thiruvalluvar statue. The shore is rocky and the sea rough, so it is for views rather than swimming.

sections.heading: How many days?
paras: Two days covers Chennai and Mahabalipuram. A full coastal loop to Rameswaram and Kanyakumari takes six to eight days, as distances are long.

safety: Do not swim at Marina beach; bathing is prohibited because of undercurrents.
Swim only at beaches with lifeguards, inside the flagged zone, and never when a red flag is up or during the monsoon.
Check cyclone warnings in October to December, when this coast is most exposed.
At Dhanushkodi and Kanyakumari, stay back from the water on rocky and windy stretches.
Surf only with a school and in suitable conditions.
packing: Light cotton clothes and a hat
A rain jacket from October to December
